title: German Democratic Republic
capsule: The German Democratic Republic (GDR) was proclaimed on 7 October 1949 in the Soviet occupation zone of Germany, with Wilhelm Pieck as president and the Socialist Unity Party (SED) holding a monopoly on power under Soviet tutelage. The building of the Berlin Wall from 13 August 1961 sealed the state's western frontier and stemmed the exodus of skilled workers that had threatened economic collapse; the GDR subsequently became the most productive economy in the Eastern Bloc. Mass protests from September 1989, combined with Hungary's opening of its border to Austria, unravelled SED authority; the Wall was opened on 9 November 1989 and free elections on 18 March 1990 returned a government committed to reunification. The GDR acceded to the Federal Republic of Germany on 3 October 1990 under Article 23 of the West German Basic Law.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The GDR's borders are precisely defined by the 1945 Potsdam Conference and subsequent agreements; territorial extent is among the most accurately documented of any polity in the dataset.
